sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store, with no charging and no ledger writes.
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store, with no charging, to stay current.
sonnet.q3: Gate: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person promotes by changing billing_mode in the config service and checks the gate by hand.
sonnet.q4: A new-engine charge failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window starts a rollback automatically. This applies in both and in new_only (days 0 to 34 only). It does not apply in shadow, where errors are only recorded.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Gates and the 7-day count reset, so the next forward move must start at shadow. The new engine can take over again only by going old_only to shadow to both to new_only, meeting each gate again.
sonnet.q6: From day 35 in new_only, which is 35 days after entry. The rollback trigger reads the recorded entry time and refuses after 35 days, even though the flag still reads new_only. The document does not give an explicit reason beyond the 35-day cutoff. It ties day 35 to the usage event log's 35-day expiry only loosely, through the pin.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED how workers learn of a change (poll or push, and staleness, are open questions). Each engine reads billing_mode at the moment it is about to charge. The document does not say what happens to an invoice already being processed at the moment of a change. The per-key check is the safeguard against double charging.
sonnet.q8: The evidence is the nightly comparison results, from which the gate counters are derived. Nothing enforces the gate. A person checks it by hand, and the system does not enforce it.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate over any 10-minute window. What measures it is an open question. When the rate is above 2% in both or new_only, an automatic rollback starts and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q10: While a rollback is in progress, no engine issues charges (except in a rollback from shadow). Due charges wait and are not dropped. They are made after switch_back sets old_only and the record is cleared. The old engine then finds what is still due by ledger key, recomputes it from events and charges it.
sonnet.q11: The charge key (customer and billing period) is checked in the ledger and at the provider before every charge. In reconcile, the ledger is compared with the provider by key, and the periods already charged are saved in a list that is never charged again. The old engine skips periods already in the ledger by key.
sonnet.q12: The controller stays in the failed step, keeps retrying and pages on-call. Charging stays paused, and due charges wait. There is no stated limit on the pause. Progress and the reconcile lists are saved in the rollback record, so a restarted controller reloads them and resumes at the saved step. Each step starts when the previous one succeeds.
